item.title: What Is Temporal Leverage?
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
How Alchemix Can Earn More Than Other CDPs

Temporal Leverage is the bonus yield you earn on Alchemix v3 because collateral set aside to repay your loan keeps earning until the moment it’s used. In most CDPs and lending markets, collateral matched to a repayment is sold right away and stops earning. In v3, it stays in your vault, working for you, right up to settlement.

In most lending systems, the collateral that repays your loan is sold as needed. When sold, you stop earning. Alchemix handles this differently. In v3, collateral in your vault position stays in the position until the moment a portion of debt is settled through redemptions.

Redemptions are a scheduled, built-in part of the system, and that schedule changes how your collateral behaves while it sits in a vault. This collateral continues to earn yield until it is redeemed, earning for longer than it would in a typical lending market. The result is what we call Temporal Leverage.

How do redemptions work in Alchemix v3?

In v3, your loan is paid down through scheduled redemptions that run through the Transmuter, working alongside the yield your collateral earns. alAsset deposits queue in the Transmuter for a fixed term, and at maturity the protocol converts collateral to fill them, applying that value against outstanding debt.

Because every redemption is scheduled in advance, the protocol knows how much collateral it will need and when, long before it needs it.

What is earmarking, and why does your collateral keep earning?

When alAssets queue in the Transmuter, the protocol earmarks an equal value of user MYT (Mix-Yield Token) collateral and debt to back the eventual redemption. Earmarking only flags the amount for redemption. It doesn’t move your collateral, and it doesn’t stop it from earning.

In most protocols, once debt is queued for repayment, the matching collateral is sold immediately and stops working.

This is where v3 breaks from typical redemption systems. In most protocols, once debt is queued for repayment, the matching collateral is sold immediately and stops working. In v3, all your collateral keeps earning yield while earmarked. Collateral only leaves your vault when the matching Transmuter position is claimed, and you collect yield on that balance right up to settlement.

That extra return is Temporal Leverage. The longer the gap between earmark and settlement, the more bonus yield you collect before the earmarked amount goes toward your debt.

Temporal Leverage vs. other CDPs

How fast do loans clear?

The redemption rate sets the pace of loan clearing. It shows the share of total system debt that redemptions repay over a year. The higher the rate, the faster loans clear. Three things move it:

  • How many alAssets are sitting in the Transmuter
  • The length of the Transmutation Time
  • Total system debt

More alAssets queued in the Transmuter raise the rate, a shorter term raises it, and more system debt lowers it. When alAssets drift below peg, arbitrage deposits grow the queue (subject to Transmuter deposit caps), so the system naturally pulls itself back towards parity.

How does Temporal Leverage affect your loan?

Positional impact depends on how much you borrow.

At very conservative LTV’s, yield can outpace redemptions. Your collateral keeps growing while your debt falls. We call this a Self-Repaying Loan, and it behaves similarly to Alchemix v2. At higher LTVs, you deleverage faster, but you can hold your leverage by re-borrowing as redemptions come through.

Either way, deleveraging costs you almost nothing. Your debt and collateral are like-kind, so redemptions repay your loan at full value.

Say you deposit 10,000 USDC, borrow 2,000 alUSD (a 20% LTV), and your MYT collateral earns 6% APR. Over a 90-day Transmutation Time, 500 alUSD of your debt is earmarked for redemption.

In a typical redemption system, 500 USDC of your collateral would be sold on day one and stop earning. In v3, it stays in your vault and earns for all 90 days, or more specifically, until the claim is finalized, which could extend beyond those 90 days.

Temporal Leverage in short

Temporal Leverage is the extra yield you earn because v3 earmarks collateral ahead of time instead of selling it on the spot. Every day between flagged and settled belongs to you.

You earn yield you would otherwise lose in other lending markets, letting your collateral work harder, for longer, while redemptions clear your debt.

item.title: Inside the Liquidation Engine of Alchemix v3
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
On most lending platforms, liquidation is a price problem. Deposit ETH, borrow against it, and if ETH falls far enough, the protocol sells your collateral to cover the loan. The market moved, and now your position is gone.

Alchemix v3 removes price from that equation. A price drop alone can't liquidate you. Only a loss in the yield strategies your collateral is invested in can. Even then, the protocol takes only part of the position, enough to bring it back to a safe ratio.

Price can’t liquidate

Your debt and collateral inside Alchemix are like-kind. ETH backs alETH, USDC backs alUSD. When you borrow, both sides of your position are denominated in the same underlying, so they move together. If ETH doubles or halves, your collateral and your debt shift by the same amount. The ratio between them stays constant.

The market price of alUSD doesn’t affect your loan either. If alUSD trades below 1.00 on a DEX, one alUSD still cancels one dollar of debt inside the Alchemist.

The 90% loan-to-value (LTV) cap is the last piece. It limits how much you can borrow against your collateral, and hitting it only stops further borrowing. Your position stays open and keeps earning.

What can liquidate

There is one path to liquidation in Alchemix v3: a drop in the value backing your collateral. Collateral is held as the Mix-Yield Token (MYT), a basket of yield strategies. If a strategy loses value through an exploit, a negative return, or its token trading below its underlying on the market (such as a liquid staking token), your loan’s backing shrinks, and your effective LTV rises.

Liquidation only becomes possible once your LTV reaches the 95% threshold. Price volatility alone cannot get you there. Each MYT is spread across several strategies, with the DAO capping the riskier ones, so a loss in one strategy reduces only part of your backing.

How liquidation works

The protocol first repays any earmarked debt on your position (the part of your debt already set aside for upcoming redemptions) using your own collateral. If that brings your LTV back under 95%, the process stops there.

If not, the protocol takes only enough collateral to bring your position back to 90% LTV, and the rest keeps earning. It closes a position in full only if the debt reaches the collateral value, or if the Alchemist as a whole goes above 95% LTV.

A liquidation fee is paid when this happens. If your collateral cannot fully cover that fee, a separate fee vault covers the difference, so the rest of the system stays whole.

You can check this directly in the vault UI. The vault shows the max borrowable LTV and liquidation threshold for your position, and if the MYT ever records a loss, the liquidation marker moves to reflect the reduced backing.

What this means for you

Because the only real risk is a loss in backing, protecting yourself comes down to knowing what is in your MYT composition and setting your LTV with room to spare.

The DAO caps how much of each MYT can go to riskier strategies: 20% in total for Aggressive, 40% for any one Moderate strategy, and 60% for Moderate and Aggressive together. Conservative strategies can make up any share.

Say you borrow at 36% LTV. If every Moderate and Aggressive strategy went to zero at once, your collateral would keep 40% of its value, and your LTV would rise to 90%, still under the 95% threshold.

Before you choose your LTV, review the strategy breakdown and risk categories in the app. The DAO can change caps and reclassify strategies, so check again when the strategy mix changes.

Day to day, most borrowers will never see a liquidation. It is a backstop for the rare case of a real loss.

Before you borrow

Liquidation is a scary word. In Alchemix v3, it is also one of the least likely things you will face. Your collateral and debt are like-kind, so when ETH or USDC moves, your LTV stays the same. The DAO caps how much of each MYT goes to riskier strategies.

Borrow with that in mind. Set an LTV with room to spare, and keep an eye on strategy mixes for your MYT.

item.title: Alchemix Q2 2026 Report Summary
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
This is a summary of the Alchemix Q2 2026 Report, which can be found in full in the Alchemix User Docs. This report provides relevant data for Q2 2026, April 1st 2026 to July 1st 2026.

The second quarter of 2026 brought many developments into the crypto space and into the Alchemix world, including the following:

In a continuation of the trend of Q1 2026, Q2 saw continued ETH depreciation and broader market turbulence resulting in Alchemix experiencing declines in treasury, deposit, and Elixir valuations. Despite the continuing downturn across nearly all crypto assets, protocol revenue grew this quarter.

  • The protocol earned approximately $329,000 in revenue for the quarter.
  • The v2 to v3 migration was completed successfully and v3 went live.
  • The Alchemix v3 bug bounty was launched with $300,000 in rewards.
  • Defi Dad invited scoopy to explain the all-new Alchemix v3.
  • The Mix-Yield Token brings diversified yield with automatic rebalancing.
  • Alchemix and the Fight for Crypto’s Soul, a podcast with scoopy and Josh.
  • Here are all the details on the new v3 Transmuter, our price stability engine.
  • Learn about our key partners and their strategies that provide yield for our Mix-Yield Tokens: Auto Finance, Morpho, Euler, Frax Finance and InfiniFi.
  • Learn how to borrow against your Mix-Yield Token position in 60 seconds.
  • Then learn how to repay your Alchemix loan in 60 seconds.
  • A short X article on the Rebirth of alAssets in Alchemix v3.
  • Our Medium article regarding ALCX, Binance and the Future.

This document is not investment advice, nor should anything herein be construed as solicitation to buy or invest. This is for informational purposes only. The discussions in this document represent a good-faith effort to effectively summarize the information that is contained in the corresponding Quarterly Report, the disclaimer of which, including, but not limited to, discussion about forward-looking statements, also applies to this document. The numbers that are being provided below, as of July 1st 2026, as well as other information disclosed in this document, are unaudited. In an effort to effectively summarize the data, this document may contain conjectures or guesses that are the authors’ alone, and do not represent any official positions, feelings or statements of the Alchemix protocol itself.

Introduction

Alchemix is a protocol for saving, borrowing, and earning fixed-yield returns. Building on the self-repaying loan it introduced in 2021, v3 combines these three functions in one app.

Conceived as a new tool for people to take advantage of the time value of money, Alchemix is tested and audited and then deployed on-chain using smart contracts to provide security, transparency, immutability, and uncensorable access to all.

Q1 2026 Lookback

Before we dive into the latest updates, the previous quarter brought interesting developments into the Alchemix world, including the following:

  • The protocol earned approximately $246,000 in revenue for the quarter.
  • yAudit has completed their audit, it’s time for the migration to Alchemix v3.
  • Alea Research has written a primer on the changes in v3.
  • Ov3rKoalafied is interviewed about Alchemix, DeFi and v3 by Immunefi.
  • Alchemix and Auto Finance hosted a networking event at ETHDenver.
  • The Alchemix v3 documentation was released for new and existing users.
  • Another v3 audit was completed, this time with an Immunefi competition.
  • As part of the v3 migration, we have an incentive for our loyal users.
  • Incentives have moved to the new ALCX-WETH Balancer V3 pool.
  • Details on the migration from v2 to v3 were released on our Medium.
  • Two AIPs were voted on in preparation for the launch of Alchemix v3.

Q2 2026 TL;DR Metrics

At the end of Q2 2026, alUSD price (0.9517) had decreased slightly and alETH price (0.9687) increased slightly compared to the previous quarter. The value of the Treasury decreased by 18.61% to $6.41M, Global Deposits decreased by 14.03% to $26.96M (including an increase of 36 ETH, or 0.3% of total ETH deposits), and the value of Elixir Contents decreased by 7.00% to $11.29M. Meanwhile, Protocol Revenue increased by 32.00% to $0.33M.

Q2 2026 Data

alAsset Prices

The main challenge for the protocol is to maintain a strong price for the alAssets.

alUSD:USDC Price

alETH:ETH Price

alAsset Utility

The image below shows the tools and protocols used within the Alchemix ecosystem, many of which provide direct use-cases for alAssets.

Specific integrations and partners are discussed in the full report.

ALCX Governance Token

The governance token of the Alchemix protocol is ALCX. It allows users to influence protocol direction by voting on submitted proposals.

As shown on the chart, the initial high token issuance rate decreased in a linear fashion, dropping to the baseline 2200 tokens emitted per week at the 3-year mark, which was in March 2024.

ALCX emissions are used to support the strategic goals of the protocol.

The protocol is still incentivizing single-sided staking, ALCX liquidity, and alAsset liquidity by using ALCX emissions. However, it has begun the transition to using emissions for the purpose of accumulating strategic assets.

The annualized inflation rate of ALCX is shown below and is very slowly decreasing in perpetuity:

Alchemix System Components

The Alchemix v3 protocol operates as a unified system for saving, borrowing, and earning fixed-yield returns. It transitions away from the v2 structure to improve capital efficiency, aggregate yield strategies, and fixed-yield opportunities. The system revolves around three core functions that users interact with through Vaults, Alchemists, and the Transmuters.

1. Vaults and Mix-Yield Tokens (MYT)

Users begin by depositing assets (such as ETH or USDC) into a Vault. Instead of being locked into a single yield farm, depositors receive Mix-Yield Tokens (MYT). Each MYT represents a proportionate share of a diversified portfolio of yield strategies curated by the Alchemix DAO. Yield accrues continuously across these multiple strategies and is reflected directly in the growing redemption value of the MYT. Users can withdraw their assets at any time without lock-ups.

2. Self-Repaying Loans (Alchemists)

As in previous versions, the Alchemist contracts handle the borrowing mechanics. Users can take out loans against their Vault deposits (MYT) by minting synthetic alAssets (alETH or alUSD). Alchemix v3 allows for highly capital-efficient borrowing, offering a Loan-to-Value (LTV) limit of up to 90% without the risk of price-based liquidations. While the user holds the alAsset loan, the underlying Vault deposit continues to earn interest across the MYT’s yield strategies. Vault yield, as well as scheduled redemptions, ensure the loan balance decreases over time. Users retain full flexibility to manually repay their loan, self-liquidate, or withdraw their principal at any time.

3. The Transmuter (Fixed Returns and alAsset Price Stability)

The Transmuter in v3 has been redesigned to offer predictable fixed-yield opportunities while actively maintaining the stability of the alAssets. Users can deposit synthetic alAssets (alETH or alUSD) into the Transmuter for a fixed term. Upon the term’s completion, the user redeems an equivalent amount of the underlying foundational asset (ETH or USDC).

Because the exchange rate is locked in at the time of deposit, the Transmuter acts as an arbitrage mechanism. If an alAsset trades below a 1:1 exchange rate on secondary markets (e.g., alUSD trades at 0.98 USDC), users are incentivized to buy the discounted alAsset and lock it in the Transmuter to redeem it for a full $1.00 USDC at the end of the term, locking in a predictable return. This systemic arbitrage provides constant buying pressure, keeping alAssets closely anchored to parity.

Elixir Contents

In Q1 2026, the Elixirs contained $12.14M in USD equivalents. At the close of Q2 2026 USD equivalents had decreased to $11.29M.

This quarter the Elixirs contracted by $0.85M (-7.00%) primarily due to the decrease in the price of Ethereum.

Treasury

A Treasury dashboard that highlights revenues and expenses, as well as assets and liabilities, can be found at https://alchemix-stats.com.

In Q1 2026 the treasury assets were valued at $7.87M and composed of stablecoin assets valued at $1.78M and $6.09M of other assets. By the end of Q2 2026 the treasury assets were valued at $6.41M and composed of stablecoin assets valued at $1.81M and $4.60M of other assets, which represents a 18.61% decrease for the quarter. The above numbers reflect non-ALCX holdings.

Protocol Revenue

The following shows protocol revenue for Q2 2026. The revenue is denominated in the USD value of the tokens earned at the time that the tokens were claimed. Included is revenue earned by the protocol’s Elixirs, and revenue earned from fees on Mainnet, Optimism, Arbitrum, a Velodrome veNFT on Optimism, and an Aerodrome veNFT on Base. This report does not include tokens whose total revenue was less than $1,000 for the quarter or revenue on chains that are not yet supported by Alchemix’s bookkeeping provider.

Deposit Metrics

This section provides numbers for user activity in the protocol’s contracts. All data is for Q2 of 2026.

Net Deposits at Quarter End

At the end of Q1 2026 net deposits consisted of Mainnet stablecoins $4.27M, Mainnet ETH $24.91M, Optimism deposits of $1.85M and Arbitrum deposits of $0.33M.

Q2 2026 net deposits consisted of Mainnet stablecoins $7.41M, Mainnet ETH $17.67M, Optimism deposits of $1.65M and Arbitrum deposits of $0.23M.

At the end of Q2 2026, net deposits on Alchemix were $26.96M, a decrease of 14.03% over the previous quarter.

Governance

There were no Governance proposals that were voted on in Q2 2026.

item.title: Alchemix on Base
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
Five years ago, Alchemix invented the Self-Repaying Loan. A loan with no interest, no repayment schedule, and no liquidations to watch. Your deposit earned yield, and that yield paid your debt down for you.

Five years later, Alchemix v3 is now live and on Base.

Alchemix v3 has three main pillars:

  • Variable-rate yield. Deposit collateral into a Mix-Yield token and earn yield across a mix of strategies curated by the Alchemix DAO. One deposit distributes your capital across several pools with varying risk levels. There are no lock-ups, and you can withdraw at any time.
  • Fixed yield. Deposit alAssets into the Transmuter for a fixed term and redeem the underlying 1:1 at maturity. You lock in your rate the moment you deposit. Exit at any time for a small fee on the unmatured portion.
  • Borrow. Your deposit backs up to 90% in alUSD or alETH, with no interest, while the collateral behind it keeps earning. Debt and collateral are like-for-like, so a move in the price of ETH or USDC can’t trigger a liquidation. Only a loss of value in the MYT can.

What’s different on Base

Alchemix v3 works the same way on Base as it does everywhere else. However, our vaults deploy a diversified set of strategies based on their chain, meaning Base will have a different vault composition adjusted for the yield sources available within the ecosystem.

Every strategy is independently audited and risk-classified before it enters a vault, with hard caps on the share of the mix that aggressive strategies can occupy. New strategies can be proposed and pushed through Alchemix governance in the near future.

Composition isn’t the only difference on Base. The siloed deployment allows us to launch with the parameters v3 was designed around.

  • Four-week terms — Transmuter terms are set per chain, and Base is launching with our shortest term length yet. Fixed-rate positions on Base will mature fast, meaning your funds aren’t locked nearly as long.
  • Faster redemption cycles — Short terms mean redemptions cycle through the system quicker. For borrowers, the debt of your position will clear faster.
  • New alAsset — Base gets its own freshly deployed alAsset alUSD.b.
  • Uncapped Transmuters — On Base there are no caps, with full Fixed-Rate capacity open on day one.

Your first Alchemix deposit

Let’s take a look at how to get started with Alchemix on Base. Head to Alchemix.fi and connect your wallet.

Navigate to Earn and select your yield profile of choice (Variable Rate for borrowing power and diversified yield, Fixed Rate for predictable term-based yield). We’ll use our Variable Rate Mixed-Yield for this example and select the Base USDC vault.

When you deposit, the vault mints a token called “MYT”, or the Mix-Yield Token. Each MYT represents your share of a portfolio of yield strategies chosen and rebalanced by the Alchemix DAO. Yield accrues continuously and shows up as growth in your MYT value.

If earning yield is all you came for, you can stop here. There are no lock-ups, and you can withdraw whenever you’d like without penalty.

Your first loan

Self-Repaying Loans are what Alchemix is known for. On the borrow page, you can take a loan against your deposit.

The protocol allows up to 90% LTV (loan-to-value), the maximum share of your collateral you can borrow against. You set your own number when you open the position. If you borrow near the cap, the position is worth checking on. Borrow well under it, and there is nothing to manage, since redemptions only move your LTV down.

Enter your borrow amount and confirm to receive the corresponding alAsset. These alAssets are Alchemix’s synthetic tokens, each backed 1:1 by the protocol.

If you are looking for liquid funds, you don’t need to handle the swap yourself. Borrow directly to the underlying asset, and the app swaps the alAsset for USDC in one transaction. If you prefer to hold the alAsset, mint it as is and swap later on the Aerodrome USDC/alUSD.b pair whenever you need to. alAssets may trade slightly below peg due to redemption mechanics; the UI will show the current rate.

Scheduled redemptions will pay your debt down over time while your collateral keeps earning. No repayments, no interest, no repayment date, and no other actions are required from you. You can repay early at any time if you want your full collateral back sooner.

For a more comprehensive walkthrough, see the borrowing tutorial in our docs or YouTube channel.

Where to go from here

You now have everything you need for your first Alchemix position. Your deposit is earning, and your loan, if you have one, is clearing itself over time.

Explore Alchemix on Base: www.alchemix.fi

Read the v3 docs to learn more: https://docs.alchemix.fi/

item.title: Based Alchemix Economic Engine
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
by Scoopy Trooples

Every healthy complex system runs in cycles. The water cycle lifts moisture from the oceans and carries it across the globe as rain, bringing life to land far from any lake or river, before that water finds its way back to the sea to begin again. The body’s circulatory system pumps blood to every tissue and organ, delivering the oxygen and nutrients that keep us alive. Cycles like these run all throughout nature. One thing they all share in common is that if the flow stops, the system dies. A pond with no inflow goes stagnant. A heart that stops pumping ends a life.

Likewise, the world’s economy works the same way. Money moves among people, businesses, and institutions, carrying resources to where they are needed. Economists call this the velocity of money, and when it slows, the economy slows with it.

DeFi is no different.

One issue that DeFi keeps trying to solve is low velocity of money onchain. DEXs live off volume, which is why so many have pushed into memecoins and launchpads that funnel activity straight into their venues. Yield aggregators take a different angle, sweeping idle funds into lending protocols, DEX LPs, and RWA vehicles so that capital ends up in the hands of whoever can put it to work. Lending markets do something similar, routing deposits toward the markets that actually need them. Innovation from DEX’s blend these approaches and allocate out-of-range liquidity to productive venues.

Alchemix is one of the protocols working on this problem. The v3 system sits atop three pillars: the Mix Yield Token (MYT), the Alchemist CDP system, and the Transmuter redemption system. Each system is integral to the others. The MYT allocates deposits to lending markets, other yield aggregators, and RWAs, so depositors earn yield without their capital sitting idle. The Alchemist turbocharges that efficiency by letting the MYT be used as collateral to borrow like-kind assets, putting even more capital into circulation on top of what was deposited. The Transmuter closes the loop, balancing debt over-expansion through fixed-term redemptions. Those redemptions double as fixed-rate zero coupon bonds against the system’s synthetic debt.

Alchemix v3 launched with a migration of long-time v2 users. Since the two systems work fundamentally differently, we eased people in by limiting velocity, keeping v3’s early behavior closer to the self repaying loans model they already knew from v2. We also started conservatively, so every part could be tested safely in production. The good news is it works exactly like we thought it would. The bad news is that the same long-horizon, conservative parameterization has left velocity low. It has come at a cost of slower growth, and synths that peg weakly. The long term plan is to gradually shorten redemption durations and let velocity rise. But moving too fast risks destabilizing the system and rattling depositors, so like everything else in this migration, that transition is happening slowly, one step at a time.

But what if we could launch somewhere we didn’t have to be sensitive to our legacy users? What if we could isolate a new instance, economically untethered from the cross-chain v3 system, and bring in new depositors carrying an entirely different set of assumptions?

Introducing Based Alchemix. Yes, Alchemix is launching on Base. This deployment is deliberately isolated from the existing ones, built around a new variant of our stablecoin synthetic asset, alUSDb (the b is for Base). Here, the parameters are deliberately tuned to maximize both velocity and efficiency. Redemptions will be fast, targeting 4 weeks. CDPs will be efficient, with 90% LTV borrowing. Even the redemption fee is set low at 10 basis points, priced for velocity, not extraction. Liquidity will be deep, with Alchemix DAO putting its Aerodrome voting power behind deep alUSDb pools. The MYT will be competitive, blending the best USDC yields Base has to offer.

Together, these form a new economic engine.

Based Alchemix is for Loopers:

With a peg expected to range between 0.996 and 0.99, looping your position multiplies your yield. Here’s how. A user deposits $10,000, borrows alUSDb against it, swaps that for USDC, and redeposits. Repeating the loop scales their principal by over 9x. A base 5% yield can become over 45% this way. That theoretical maximum sits right at the edge of the liquidation zone though, so in practice most loopers will run 4–6x leverage and keep a healthy buffer. There will be a tool to make this a simple one-click process in our UI.

Based Alchemix is for Fixed-Rate-Yield Seekers:

Fixed-rate yield is one of Alchemix v3’s core products, and it works though fixed-duration redemptions. When alUSDb trades at a discount, that discount becomes an arbitrage opportunity. alUSDb is meant to trade roughly 1:1 with USDC, but when the peg wobbles, it can be bought on the open market and then redeemed 1:1 for USDC once the term is up. For example, if alUSDb falls to $0.99 and redemption takes a month, a user can buy it at that discount and convert it to USDC in that time span, earning 1% in one month, roughly 12% annualized. These opportunities move with the market and yields will vary, but once you’ve bought in, your rate is locked at your execution price. Redemptions are uncapped: no queue, no gating, just the 4-week term as the only throttle. We expect the market to demand at least what US 1-month T-Bills yield, plus some unknown DeFi premium, which is roughly why the peg should sit in that 0.99–0.996 range. And if a wave of leveraged borrowing ever pushes the peg below the floor, it is the fixed-rate seeker who feasts: the discount widens, and the redemption still pays 1:1.

Based Alchemix is for LPs:

The interplay between loopers and fixed-rate-seekers creates a high velocity environment. Loopers sell alUSDb into the market to open their loop, pushing the price down; fixed-rate seekers step in to buy the dip, locking in yield at a discount. That push and pull drives real volume through alUSDb pairs on DEXs. Loopers dump, fixed-rate seekers defend, and the peg finds its way back to target. As an LP, you earn fees off every bit of that back-and-forth. Additionally, the risk of LPing alUSDb markets is bounded. If the peg breaks, you either wait a brief moment for an arbitrageur to close the gap, or withdraw and redeem the alUSDb 1:1 for USDC through the 4-week window. Your worst case is the wait, not the price.

Based Alchemix is an Economic Engine:

What we’ve described so far is a high-churn, high-velocity, high-efficiency system, and yes that is true. But the real magic behind this engine’s growth is a timing mismatch. When a looper opens a large position, the arbitrage that corrects any resulting peg pressure locks in immediately, even when the redemption behind it takes 4 weeks to settle. That 4-week term means each arbitrage dollar can turn over up to 13 times per year, and at any given moment, roughly 4 weeks of looper sell flow is sitting patiently in the redemption queue, waiting to be redeemed 1:1. That patience is what lets more loopers in, which opens more arbitrage opportunities, which drives more volume to DEX pools, which makes LPing more profitable, which deepens those pools, which makes more room for the next round of loopers. The system feeds itself. And it is entirely positive sum: none of that yield is conjured from inside the loop. The MYT earns real yield from outside the system (Base lending markets and other strategies), and routes it to the people taking on duration and peg risk.

The engine scales with the capital that wants it. Its bottlenecks are real, but they grow alongside it: the yield capacity of the venues the MYT allocates to, the pool of patient capital willing to sit out a redemption, the depth of the DEX pools themselves. Past that, the only real limit is how many people we can bring in. Savers who see they can access levered yield will use as much of that capacity as they can get at a good price, and every looper who pushes the peg down hands an arbitrageur a reason to defend it, freeing up room for the next looper. Round and round it goes, each turn compounding on the last. This is the only yield farm that gets better the more people and capital show up.

Growing this ecosystem has knock-on effects for the rest of Base too. As the MYT allocates capital, it deepens lending markets and other active strategies, which expands borrowing capacity across Base DeFi, which draws more money onchain. As the protocol grows, it pushes more volume to DEXs, which pays LPs to show up, which pulls in still more capital. Everything is additive, and everyone wins. Our success becomes everyone’s success, breathing life into the ecosystem and stimulating the circulatory system of its economy.

Join Us:

There are several ways to participate and earn in the v3 system. Will you be a looper, an arbitrageur, or an LP? Either way you play it, there will be economic opportunity waiting at your fingertips.

Get started: https://alchemix.fi

Learn more: https://docs.alchemix.fi

item.title: Alchemix v3 Journal #1: Welcome v3
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the first edition of the new and improved Alchemix Journal! This is being rebuilt and redesigned from the ground up to coincide with the release of Alchemix v3. You can expect one of these every few months when we have interesting things to share.

Where we are

Alchemix v3 has been live since April 18th, 2026. Getting there took the largest operation in Alchemix history: 6,413 positions migrated across 3 chains, with nearly 20,000 transactions, $4.87M in stablecoins, and 12,107 ETH moved, all without a single user lifting a finger. V3 opened with limited deposit caps, with everything verified by the team against live conditions, and caps were subsequently raised in stages through early May.

You can now borrow up to 90% against your collateral while it keeps earning. That collateral is held as the Mix-Yield Token, which spreads it across a curated basket of risk-adjusted strategies. The Fixed-Duration Transmuter redeems alAssets 1:1 on a known date. Three months in, the system is doing what it was built to do.

From a security standpoint, v3 launched after audits from Spearbit/Cantina, Nethermind, and yAudit, an Immunefi audit competition, and an independent review of the earmarking and transmutation accounting by alpeh_v. Furthermore, there is an ongoing active Immunefi bounty of up to $150,000.

For any users who are new to, or not very familiar with, how Alchemix works, we suggest getting started with the v3 docs. These docs include an introduction to the protocol, along with what it is, how it works, tutorials, and more. And for more advanced users, the docs include technical sections describing how the Alchemix v3 modules and contracts work.

The MYT basket expanded

The launch of Alchemix v3 included the development and introduction of a new token type, the MYT (Mix-Yield Token). The MYTs are a core component of how v3 works and represent one of the biggest design departures from Alchemix v2. For more on why Alchemix decided to go this route, please read this.

Each Mix-Yield Token is only as strong as the strategies inside it, and the basket has expanded steadily since launch. ETH and USDC mixes live on Ethereum Mainnet, Arbitrum, and Optimism. The vaults at launch routed through Aave, Yearn, Euler, Fluid, Auto Finance, and Lido’s wstETH are set to be auto-rebalanced by the DAO soon.

Three strategies have joined since the v3 launch: Staked Frax ETH (sfrxETH) and Ether.fi (weETH) on the ETH side, and infiniFi’s iUSD on the stablecoin side. Each strategy adds a new source of yield to the mix, deepening diversification on both sides of the basket.

Every strategy is audited before it is whitelisted, in an ongoing arrangement with Nethermind, so the basket can grow without the risk profile drifting. Compositions and weights will eventually be adjusted by DAO vote, so treat any list as a snapshot and check the live baskets before depositing.

Learn more about the MYT.

A stronger foundation for alAssets

The most significant change of the launch was in how alAssets behave. alUSD and alETH are synthetic debt tokens, always backed by at least 1 unit of collateral and always worth 1 unit of debt inside Alchemix. The open market usually prices them slightly below, a side effect of borrowers selling what they mint. The Alchemix v3 Transmuter now has a predictable and updatable debt redemption schedule. v3’s scheduled redemptions convert that small, external discount into a predictable, dated 1:1 exit. This means a predictable yield for users who want to arbitrage the market discounts on alAsset prices.

alAssets are also picking up utility outside the protocol, starting with the Euler 4-way market. For the first time, you can borrow USDC or WETH against your alAssets: deposit ETH into Alchemix, borrow alETH, then borrow again against that alETH through the Euler vault. alAssets can now work alongside their underlying; more integrations are being explored, including Pendle markets and perps collateral.

Supporting this push, a partnership with Chronicle is bringing dedicated oracles to each alAsset, giving integrators reliable price feeds and making alAssets fully composable across DeFi.

Learn more about alAssets.

Mix-Yield Tokens arrive on Pendle

The integration list is already growing. You can now deposit directly into the ETH and USDC Mix-Yield Tokens through Pendle, a DeFi protocol that tokenizes future yield. This is the first of many DeFi integrations coming to v3. One deposit and a diversified set of DAO-curated yield strategies are working for you. Deposit into Mix USDC or Mix ETH straight from Pendle’s app.

The Alchemix Ecosystem vault

Alongside the core Mix-Yield Tokens, there is now an Alchemix Ecosystem vault. Built on Lagoon, a platform for curated on-chain vaults, it puts your deposit to work across Alchemix ecosystem strategies. You will find it in the Ecosystem tab, and it is worth a look if you want exposure a step beyond the core vaults. The idea is a single deposit that follows the stronger yields across the Alchemix ecosystem without active management. Check the live APR in the app before depositing.

Swap and bridge, now in the app

You no longer have to leave Alchemix to move between assets or chains. The in-app Swap trades directly between tokens, for example, ETH into alETH, with routing handled by aggregators such as Enso and LI.FI behind the scenes. The Bridge moves your tokens across Ethereum Mainnet, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Linea, and Metis, and can send them to a different wallet if you need. It keeps swapping and bridging within a single interface instead of being scattered across third-party sites. A small routing fee applies.

Under the hood, the alAsset bridges themselves were rebuilt for v3 earlier this year, with cross-chain messages now verified by independent networks under the same 2-of-3 confirmation standard as before.

Fewer steps, thanks to Enso

Enso now powers a set of one-click flows that remove manual steps in our UI. You can now borrow USDC or ETH directly against your deposit, rather than borrowing an alAsset and swapping it yourself afterward. The Transmuter now accepts more than just alAssets: deposit USDC or WETH straight in, and Enso routes it into a transmutation position for you. That means fewer transactions to reach the position you actually want.

Moving to Phase Two: Sustainable growth

Phase One of the v3 launch is complete. The Transmuter’s first major cycle has concluded, and as those redemptions settle, deposit capacity opens up. Fresh space opened on July 23rd.

Phase Two is about sustainable growth. Transmuter terms have been extended, with most now around 9 months. Terms vary by asset and chain, and the team continues to tune them, so check the Fixed Yield page for current terms. Longer terms let us scale fixed-term deposit capacity while lightening the impact on the redemption rate for existing borrowers. To protect that structure, the Transmuter early-exit fee rose to 3% on July 15th. This fee only applies to any portion of a term that hasn’t fully matured at withdrawal.

The target we are building toward is an uncapped Transmuter with short-duration transmutations. Caps, fees, and terms can change at any time, and major changes will be announced on our socials.

Other updates

We gave the v3 docs a major refresh in July. Restructured navigation, improvements on nearly every page, deployed contract addresses, and a cleaner reading experience throughout.

You can visit the docs here.

Rewards have also returned to the ALCX/WETH pool on Balancer. With their veBAL system wound down, we now run direct incentives via Merkl.

The Numbers

This is a summary of the protocol’s financial state since the launch of v3. If you want to dive a bit deeper, the full accounting lives in the quarterly financial reports.

TVL is roughly $30.4M, compared with $28.4M in net deposits at the end of Q1, indicating a positive trend since launch despite the bear market. alAsset pegs are healthy, and ALCX emissions remain in their long-tail phase at 2,200 tokens per week. This rate has been held since March 2024, so percentage inflation continues to decline as supply grows.

For context, the most recent full report (Q1 2026, which closed just before v3 launched) reflected a broad market downturn. Protocol revenue was $0.25M for the quarter, and the treasury was $7.87M, both pulled down by the market decline. The team is currently targeting $100M in TVL, which at current rates would generate roughly $800K a year in revenue for the treasury and open the door to revenue sharing through vqALCX.

The first full post-launch quarter report is coming soon.

Learning Corner

Why alAssets trade below 1:1, and why that is fine

When a borrower mints alUSD (or alETH) and sells it for working capital, that selling pushes the market price slightly below a dollar. Inside Alchemix, nothing changes: your alUSD still repays a full dollar of debt. The gap is strictly external and actually represents an opportunity.

Turning it into yield is straightforward. You market buy alUSD or alETH below face value and deposit it into the Transmuter, which locks it for a set term. While it is locked, the protocol earmarks an equal value of MYT collateral from borrowers to back your claim. At maturity, you receive the full 1:1 value in MYT, which unwraps to the underlying asset. Your return is the spread at which you purchased, over the term you waited; all three figures are known the moment you deposit. You can exit early, but a fee applies, and you forfeit part of the fixed outcome.

That is the mechanism behind fixed yield in the app. Users have no leverage or liquidations to manage.

It is worth noting that each chain’s Transmuter has a deposit cap, so users are advised to verify available capacity before purchasing alAssets.

For a full walkthrough of how a transmutation flows from deposit to maturity, please check out the following Tweet: Transmuter introduction.

To check live terms, discounts, and remaining capacity on your preferred chain, please check out the Fixed Yield page in our dApp.

The wider market

Ideally, we would have more to say about the broader market, but we look around and see that the market is well into a bear season, and we find ourselves with little new to say.

Exchanges are becoming more selective. Altcoin liquidity is thinner, listing thresholds are higher, and volume is concentrated in a small number of large-cap assets. That pressure is affecting much of DeFi, and it is the context for the Binance news below.

Youtube Tutorials

And if you prefer video, our YouTube channel has short v3 tutorials covering everything from taking a loan to earning fixed yield with the Transmuter and the MYT.

Watch the tutorials.

Token and Governance

The Binance delisting

On June 26, Binance announced it will delist ALCX spot pairs, which was not welcome news. Delistings affect holders, liquidity, and perception, and Alchemix takes them seriously.

An exchange listing is a dramatic difference from a functioning protocol, though. v3 is live and healthy. Deposits, Self-Repaying Loans, and Transmuter flows all operate as they did the day before, and nothing about the product has changed. ALCX remains available on several CEXs, such as Coinbase and Kraken, as well as through self-custody, which we recommend for any ALCX that users hold.

Read the full statement.

ICYMI

v3 itself was governance in action. If you missed the votes that made it happen, catch up on AIP-122 (the v3 Launch Proposal and Initial Parameters) and AIP-123 (The Great v2 to v3 Migration), both covered in Governance Update #55.

With vqALCX and On-Chain Governance in development, expect this section to get much busier in future editions.

Community

Mana has concluded

The Mana migration program has concluded, and the snapshot is locked. Users who migrated to v3 share a pot of 10,000 ALCX, allocated proportionally to Mana earned.

Transmutation

Collectr’s latest edition, Transmutation, was created in collaboration with Alchemix, with art by OHNE HALS. It is available to mint only through August, so if you want one on your wall, now is the time.

Check out the mint details.

v3, from the outside looking in

If you want an outside read on v3, Alea Research, an independent DeFi research firm, has published the first two reports in a dedicated series covering the protocol’s history, Transmuter and MYT mechanics, and the case for predictable yield.

Read the perspective report.

Read the deep dive report.

Other

And for something to listen to, Scoopy joined DeFi Dad on the Edge Podcast for a full v3 breakdown, from v1’s self-repaying loans to why v3 took years to build.

Watch the Edge Podcast.

And a returning fun fact for longtime readers: since inception, gALCX has now automatically compounded over 73,497 ALCX for its holders. When this stat last appeared in the old newsletter, the count stood at 61,379.

This Newsletter is provided for informational purposes only and does not constitute any kind of advice. Use cryptocurrencies and Decentralized Finance (DeFi) at your own risk.

item.title: Diverse, risk-adjusted DeFi yield
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
Earning good yield on-chain usually means managing it yourself. Several positions, several protocols, and constantly checking rates. The Mix-Yield Token wraps that work into a single token.

What the Mix-Yield Token (MYT) is

In Alchemix v2, your deposit was tied to a single strategy. You earned whatever yield that one source generated, your risk tracked that one source, and diversifying meant opening and managing several positions yourself. If a better rate appeared elsewhere, moving to it was up to you.

The Mix-Yield Token combines several positions into a single token, spread across many strategies at once. It is an ERC-4626 vault built on a custom Alchemix implementation of Morpho Vaults V2.

When you deposit ETH or USDC into Alchemix, it is wrapped into mixETH or mixUSD. Each token represents your share of a curated basket of yield strategies, and that share grows as the strategies earn. There are no lock-ups. Yield compounds continuously, and you can redeem for your principal plus accrued yield at any time.

Each MYT holds several yield sources at once, with the Alchemix DAO choosing those strategies, setting their target weights, and rebalancing as markets move.

How mixETH and mixUSD work

When you deposit ETH or USDC, the vault mints you shares of mixETH or mixUSD and routes the assets across several strategies. As they earn, the value of each MYT rises, so the longer you hold, the more each token is worth.

Caps limit how much any single strategy can hold, which spreads risk across the basket while keeping liquidity available for entering and exiting on demand. You earn from higher-yielding strategies without concentrating your deposit in any one of them.

Risk tiers and caps

Diversification on its own is not automatically safer, so every strategy in mixETH and mixUSD is risk-classified as Conservative, Moderate, or Aggressive.

The DAO caps how much of the vault the riskier tiers can hold, both in total and per individual strategy, so no single protocol can dominate the allocation. The live composition, tiers, and caps are always published in the dApp, so you can see exactly what your deposit is exposed to at any time.

How users benefit

mixETH and mixUSD are yield products. You deposit, earn a diversified, auto-compounding yield, and redeem whenever you like.

If you are a passive holder, you get access to a diversified, auto-compounding yield wrapped into one token. No manual re-staking, no moving funds between protocols to chase the better rate.

Borrowers get a safer and more predictable yield profile for their Self-Repaying Loans. All collateral earns yield, even with an active loan.

DAOs and treasuries can park idle ETH or USDC for blended On-Chain yield and still borrow against the same assets when they need liquidity without selling their core positions.

Strategy curators can also benefit. Once the DAO transitions to full on-chain governance, designers can submit new ERC-4626 modules for DAO approval.

They also back your loans

Borrowing against mixETH or mixUSD is a separate, optional decision.

In most lending protocols, the collateral you lock sits idle as a cost until you repay. In Alchemix, your collateral keeps earning the entire time it backs your loan. As scheduled redemptions reconcile debt from your collateral, the yield that collateral keeps earning offsets what redemptions draw out.

The risk profile carries over too. When your MYT backs a loan, liquidations cannot be triggered by market price movements. They only happen if the MYT itself loses backing, such as a strategy reporting real losses. The baskets’ risk profile is your own risk profile, and the tier caps give you a concrete basis for choosing an LTV that keeps your position safe even if the higher-risk strategies experience losses.

Where the MYT is heading

The MYT’s composition is governed, not fixed, so it changes over time. Once the transition to on-chain governance is complete, new strategies can be proposed and voted on. Weights can then shift as conditions change, and each chain can run its own variant based on what is available and the risk profile. There are currently one ETH-denominated and one USDC-denominated MYT on each supported chain, specifically Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Optimism.

The baskets you can find today in the dApp are a starting point. As Alchemix continues to coordinate with partners, the set of yield sources behind every alAsset gets deeper and better diversified. In the future, Alchemix DAO will fully handle this process, adjusting allocations as conditions shift so that MYT holders maintain a healthy risk-adjusted yield at all times.

The layer underneath

Users are already familiar with alAssets, but mixETH and mixUSD are the layer beneath them. It is the deposits that back them, and the collateral the Transmuter draws from to settle redemptions at maturity.

The asset you deposit does not change once it is converted to MYT. What changes is that it stops sitting idle and starts earning.

item.title: Master DeFi’s new fixed yield primitive
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
The Transmuter is Alchemix v3’s peg stability engine and a source of fixed yield for everyone. It converts discounted alAssets to their counterparts at a 1:1 ratio in a fixed time frame.

The basic premise

Within Alchemix, one alUSD is always worth one USDC, and one alETH is always worth one ETH, even when the market prices them lower. The Transmuter lets anyone capture this arbitrage over a set period of time.

You deposit alUSD or alETH. These are locked for a term set by the DAO, and at maturity, you receive one unit of the underlying asset for every alAsset you deposit. The deposited alAssets are then burned.

The 1:1 rate is guaranteed. You only need to wait out the transmutation period, which is known before you enter the position.

Where returns come from

Borrowers mint alAssets at face value and often sell them for working capital, which pushes the market price below par. Inside Alchemix, one alUSD still settles one dollar of debt, no matter where it trades. The gap between the discounted market price and the Transmuter’s 1:1 payout is a fixed return you can lock in.

An example: alUSD is trading at 0.96 with a 90-day term. You swap 10,000 USDC for around 10,416 alUSD on your DEX of choice. Deposit it, wait the term, and receive 10,416 USDC at maturity. That is 416 USDC, about 4.16% over three months, or roughly 16.6% annualized.

What you can do with it

Hold USDC or ETH and want a fixed rate? You can enter straight from USDC or ETH in the UI, which buys the alAssets for you under the hood. Keep an eye on the alAsset price in the UI sub-menu. When the discount widens, head to the Fixed Yield page and lock in the rate. Every deposit also pulls alAssets back toward peg.

Liquidity providers get a predictable exit. If the peg widens, an LP can rotate out of their pool, deposit into the Transmuter, and redeem their alAssets at full value instead of absorbing the spread.

DAOs and Treasuries can use stable reserves to earn a known return with no rate risk.

What v3 changes

Why can v3 guarantee this when v2 couldn’t? The v2 Transmuter already redeemed alAssets 1:1, what it lacked was a way to schedule an exit.

In v2, the capital that settled redemptions arrived opportunistically, from yield harvests, repayments and liquidations flowing through the protocol. The settlement rate depended on protocol-wide activity. It worked, but it was unpredictable and slow-moving, and as a result didn’t scale well.

v3 changes this by introducing scheduled redemptions. When alAssets are queued in the Transmuter, the protocol earmarks an equivalent amount of borrower collateral backing that debt. That collateral then settles at maturity, creating a defined exit path instead of v2’s open-ended timeframe.

That single change makes the rest of v3 viable. Fixed-duration Transmuter exits, 90% LTV vaults, and temporal leverage all sit downstream of scheduled redemptions. For you as a depositor, it means a guaranteed 1:1 payout on a known date with a predictable yield.

Things to weigh before you enter

Capacity is per chain, with each Transmuter having its own deposit cap. If the one on your chain is full, you may need to bridge alAssets elsewhere to deposit, so always check available capacity before you buy.

The Transmuter gives you a full 1:1 value, but the position vests over the Transmuter term. You can claim early if you need to, taking the portion that has already vested at 1:1, and the unvested alAsset portion back, minus an early-exit fee (set by governance) on that unvested portion. Early exit means giving up part of the fixed-rate outcome.

Edge cases worth knowing

If bad debt exists in the Alchemist (from an exploit, for example), redemptions pay out pro-rata (say 0.97:1) until the debt is restored. You can claim with the haircut, or leave your claim unclaimed and redeem the full 1:1 once the debt clears.

Your payout arrives as MYT, which normally unwraps to USDC or ETH immediately. If conditions are poor and the UI flags high unwrap slippage, withdraw the MYT instead, let it keep earning yield, and unwrap later through the UI.

The takeaway

The Transmuter ensures that all alAssets are functionally worth 1:1 to their underlying assets. It tightens the peg, gives holders a guaranteed way out, and turns a market discount into a fixed return.

item.title: ALCX, Binance and the future
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
On June 26th, Binance announced they will delist ALCX spot pairs.

This is not welcome news, and we won’t pretend otherwise. Delistings hurt holders, liquidity, and perception. We are taking it very seriously.

What caused the delisting?

The short answer is: we do not know the specific trigger. We have been in close contact with Binance throughout and met every request they made of us. When ALCX was added to their monitoring list, they were unable to provide us with any further information as to the best route to fix this, apart from, “Keep on building, which we did.

What does this mean?

What we do not want is to confuse exchange mechanics with protocol health.

Alchemix v3 is live. The protocol is functioning. Deposits, Self-Repaying Loans, and Transmuter flows are all operating normally. If you use Alchemix, nothing about the product has changed. ALCX also remains available on other CEXs such as Coinbase and Kraken, and through self-custody, which we always recommend for any ALCX balances.

The reason the distinction matters is simple: ALCX is a DeFi-native governance and incentive token. Like a lot of long-tail tokens, it faces the same market pressure that led to this delisting: thinner altcoin liquidity, tighter exchange thresholds, and turnover concentrated in a handful of large-cap names.

We have chosen not to chase short-term optics. Alchemix did not pay to be listed on Binance (or any other exchange), and does not have plans to start doing so. The playbook of spending treasury on inflating surface-level volume and trying to buy back a listing is a route many protocols take, but it is not one we follow. Those programs decay quickly and divert capital from the only thing that makes a protocol durable: real usage and real revenue.

Alchemix v3 revenue is ramping up. We have an initial goal of hitting at least $100 million in TVL, which would generate approximately $800,000 in annual revenue at current rates.. That revenue flows into a transparent treasury deployed across strategic positions, governance tokens, and liquidity operations that support protocol growth. We publish public quarterly financial reports that detail all of this.

ALCX was launched without presales or VC allocations. The majority of supply goes to the people who build and use the protocol: contributors, stakers, and liquidity providers. Emissions are in a fixed long-tail phase of 2,200 ALCX per week, so percentage inflation continues to fall as supply grows.

There is a clear job for the token: coordinate governance and incentives around a protocol that keeps working and keeps shipping.

What’s next?

We keep building.

Alchemix v3 expands the design space for Self-Repaying Loans. We will keep growing alAsset utility across DeFi, and keep publishing what we earn, what we spend, and where the treasury is deployed.

We also have grand plans for the future of ALCX in the form of vqALCX. This is now fully specced and in active development, including on-chain governance which is being prepared for audit soon. These updates mark a foundational upgrade of our token, which will enable fully on-chain governance and revenue share.

A delisting is a moment to reassess, not to abandon the plan. The plan has always been to build a protocol that generates sustainable revenue and to keep ALCX tied into that plan.

That has not changed.

If you have questions, we are in Discord. We pride ourselves in fostering an open and honest dialog with our community as well as being positive-sum players in the defi space. We truly believe that we have built one of the more innovative and useful tools in the defi space, and we are excited to continue our traditions of innovation, security, and openness.

We will keep the updates coming, and are very much looking forward to what the future has in store.

item.title: The Rebirth of alAssets
item.dc:creator: Alchemix Finance
item.content:encoded:
Since Alchemix launched, alAssets have been the backbone of Self-Repaying Loans. The alAssets always worked, but there was work to be done.

From the start of alUSD and alETH’s existence, the protocol valued each alAsset at one unit of its underlying. The open market, on the other hand, often didn’t. Higher vault demand created large discounts, variable Transmuter timelines created unpredictable redemptions, and LPs absorbed impermanent loss. The assets functioned, but they were inefficient; optimization was needed.

v3 has solved this problem by introducing fixed-duration transmutations.

What alAssets really are

alUSD and alETH are synthetic debt tokens, not algorithmic stablecoins.

Algorithmic stablecoins rely on a balancing act of minting and burning based on price signals. alAssets are different: trust is rooted in collateral. Every alAsset is backed by at least one unit of its underlying value, held as MYT collateral inside the Alchemist, and offsets exactly one unit of debt inside Alchemix at face value.

The market price typically floats slightly below face value, but the protocol’s redemption logic does not. The truth is, alAssets are always backed and redeemable for 1 unit of underlying collateral.

The discount was never the problem

Market discounts on alAssets are healthy and part of the design. It creates an arbitrage for traders to buy below par and close the spread, and it lets borrowers access liquidity while still earning yield on their full principle. When borrowers mint alAssets at face value to sell them on the open market for working capital, the resulting sell pressure pushes the price below par. Inside Alchemix, the alAsset still settles 1:1 against debt, meaning the discount is external only.

What was missing was a proactive way to close the gap. The v2 Transmuter allowed 1:1 redemption, but relied on yield harvests, repayments, and liquidations to fund it. There was no scheduled movement of borrower collateral into the Transmuter, so settlements happened only when revenue allowed. This made transmutation times unpredictable.

v3 fixed this by introducing redemptions. When alAssets queue in the Transmuter, the protocol earmarks an equivalent value of vault collateral (the Mix-Yield Token that aggregates Alchemix’s curated yield strategies) that backs debt. After maturity and upon claim, the earmarked collateral is converted into the underlying asset and used to settle user debt, and service redemptions. This replaces the open-ended v2 transmutation period with something predictable. Fixed-duration transmutations.

When you deposit, you already know how much you will receive, the rate, and the date you can claim it.

So, who benefits?

LPs benefit twice. Strong demand within the Transmuter helps maintain closer price parity for alAssets across secondary markets. This alignment reduces divergence in alAsset pools, compressing impermanent loss and keeping pool yields competitive.

The Transmuter also protects against impermanent loss. If the peg widens, an LP can rotate out of the pool, deposit into the Transmuter, and exit at full 1:1 value rather than absorbing the spread. The protocol guarantees a redemption path that doesn’t depend on where the market prices the asset on any given day. That is the kind of certainty liquidity providers have long asked for in synthetic asset systems, and it is now built into the mechanics rather than promised by a market maker.

What does the future look like?

The Transmuter ensures the peg is stronger. The other improvement is utility. The more reasons there are to hold alAssets rather than sell them, the less downward pressure the market sees, and the tighter the peg stays before the Transmuter even has to engage. Peg health and asset utility complement each other.

The alAsset roadmap from here is about building these reasons to hold. The Euler 4-way market is a first major step in that goal, allowing you to borrow USDC and wETH against alAssets, which is the first time Alchemix has offered cross-borrowing using alAssets. Deposit ETH, borrow alETH, then borrow USDC against that alETH through Euler. This allows alAssets to work alongside their underlying instead of getting sold the moment they are minted.

Beyond that, we’re working towards using alAssets as collateral for borrowing elsewhere in DeFi. Potential integrations include: incorporating custom Pendle markets, and integrating with perps as quote or margin assets. The strongest integrations may come from protocols that utilize alAssets in interesting ways, such as by tying into predictable redemptions.

Looking forward

The v3 Transmuter represents a fundamental shift in how alAssets operate. By enhancing capital efficiency and predictability across minting, settlement, and trading, alAssets have been significantly improved without changes to the assets themselves. v3 establishes a more resilient alAsset foundation, setting the stage for the next phase of protocol expansion.
